title: B2B procurement under a master services agreement
instance: Carried from Nicole’s page, Case 2. Named on Oct 13 but not shown; unreviewed until the async round (Nicole [01:04:44], [01:05:03]). Was “UC1 · 2” before the RFP renumbering.

A.label: company delegates through an approver
A.sub: approved vendors · no hop widens the authority · caps a separate note

A2.label: the approver sets the agent's scope
A2.sub: a purchase order reference · per-order and monthly caps

B.label: the seller's profile asks for the legal entity on the MSA, verified
B.sub: the price depends on it, so the 402 must ask before the payload is signed · the answer: the signed payload plus the entity and the delegation chain

C.label: the wallet address is the identifier anchor
C.sub: the wallet alone does not say which company

C2.label: the identifier is linked to the legal entity (4.2.1); the delegation chain travels with it
C2.sub: an LEI or domain, verifiable against a register

E.label: AP matches the PO; the auditor tests the caps
E.sub: record kept for both · cap evidence cites 4.3.2

differs: Differs from K0 in A (a two-hop delegation) and B (the legal entity must be known before settlement because it sets the price).
slots: Company, through an approver, to the agent
From Nicole’s page: approved vendors, per-order and monthly caps, a purchase order. The caps are drawn as a note, not in the label (Alfred [00:37:59]).
Is this the legal entity on the MSA?
Nicole’s page puts this before settlement because the contract rate depends on it. Fields dial: the legal entity. Assurance dial: verified against a register.
The wallet is the anchor; the legal entity and the chain link to it
The wallet alone does not say which company; the entity link (4.2.1) and the delegation chain do.

Nicole’s page draws an Auditor lane and gives AP its own evidence need. Here both are relying parties on the record, not lanes. Cap evidence is RFP 4.3.2 (multi-payment mandates), present in the Nov 9 export.
footer: If the vendor learns which company it is dealing with only after settlement, the agent pays list price and the difference turns up in reconciliation (Nicole’s page).
A delegation chain in A, the legal entity before settlement in B, the wallet in C with the entity link.
Issued: a legal entity, verifiable against a register.
